title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the Past

questions.prompt: Three of these verbs take the regular ending -ed in the simple past. Which one does NOT?

options.text: wait
drink
talk
decorate

questions.explanation: The verb drink is irregular: it changes shape and becomes drank, so no ending is ever added to it. The three others are regular, and each one simply follows its own spelling line: waited with -ed, talked with -ed, and decorated with -d because it already ends in e.

questions.prompt: Read: "Last Sunday was Mother's Day. My father bought a perfume, my sister wrote a card and I prepared the breakfast." Which sentence is correct?

options.text: The father wrote a card.
The sister bought a perfume.
The father bought a perfume.
The sister prepared the breakfast.

questions.explanation: The text gives each person one action: the father bought the perfume, the sister wrote the card, and the one who speaks prepared the breakfast. The three other sentences swap two of those people, and the verbs keep their past shapes whoever does the action.

questions.prompt: Meriem reads the three past verbs baked, played and counted. Which sentence about their final -ed is true?

options.text: baked ends in /d/, played ends in /ɪd/, counted ends in /t/
baked ends in /t/, played ends in /d/, counted ends in /ɪd/
baked ends in /ɪd/, played ends in /t/, counted ends in /d/
baked ends in /t/, played ends in /ɪd/, counted ends in /d/

questions.explanation: Bake ends in the quiet sound k, so the ending is the quiet /t/; play ends in a vowel sound, which shakes the throat, so the ending is /d/; and count already ends in t, so a whole syllable appears and the ending is /ɪd/. The three other lines move those sounds from one verb to another, and only the sound just before the ending decides.

questions.prompt: Three of these past verbs end with the syllable /ɪd/. Which one does NOT?

options.text: waited
counted
decorated
danced

questions.explanation: The verb dance ends in the quiet sound s, not in t or d, so nothing forces a new syllable and the ending is simply /t/. Wait, count and decorate all end in the sound t, and nothing can be glued to a t, so each of them gains the whole syllable /ɪd/.

questions.prompt: Nadia tells the class where she spent her day. Which of these sentences is completely correct?

options.text: Yesterday I was at my grandmother's house and I ate a big cake.
Yesterday I was at my grandmother's house and I eated a big cake.
Yesterday I was at my grandmother's house and I ated a big cake.
Yesterday I were at my grandmother's house and I ate a big cake.

questions.explanation: Two past forms must hold at once: with I the verb be becomes was, and the irregular verb eat becomes ate. The forms "eated" and "ated" add the regular ending to a verb that refuses it, and "I were" takes the shape that belongs to you, we and they.

questions.prompt: The pupils repeat what their teacher told them on the eleventh of January. Which of these sentences is completely correct?

options.text: On Children's Day the teacher say that every child has the right to education.
On Children's Day the teacher sayed that every child has the right to education.
On Children's Day the teacher said that every child has the right to education.
On Children's Day the teacher said that every child have the right to education.

questions.explanation: The verb say is irregular and becomes said in the past, and every child is one child, so the structure is has the right to. The first sentence leaves say in the present, "sayed" adds the regular ending to an irregular verb, and the last one gives one single child the verb have, which belongs to I, you, we and they.
